chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the mature/divorced or widowed woman who proposes marriage to herself, he (peace be upon him) said: She has more authority over herself; she may entrust her affair to whomever she wishes, provided he is a match, after she has previously married a man.

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنَفْسِهَا: She has more authority/control over herself
key_terms.الثَّيِّب: A mature woman who has previously been married
key_terms.تَخْطُبُ إِلَى نَفْسِهَا: She proposes marriage to herself (managing her own suit)

ai.seo_question: Does a divorced or widowed woman need a guardian to marry in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a *thayyib* (mature woman who has previously consummated a marriage) possesses full autonomy to contract her own marriage without a *wali*, provided the suitor is her equal (*kufu*). This ruling distinguishes her status from an *unthayyib* (virgin), whose marriage typically requires guardian consent, thereby establishing a key precedent in Shia jurisprudence for female agency in marital contracts.
